_meta.note: Three vendors = the exact Air Force ANPI slate (Antares, Radiant, Westinghouse). Selecting the third vendor was not a judgment call: DoD already paired these three against three named bases in April 2026.

vendors.name: Antares Nuclear
vendors.notes: Antares plants require no connection to the commercial power grid or specialised infrastructure to deploy. Selection driven by JBSA's utility infrastructure, land availability and critical mission requirements. Under the DOE Reactor Pilot Program, Antares' Mark-0 test reactor reached zero-power fuelled criticality at Idaho National Laboratory on 2026-06-04 — one of the first three pilot reactors to meet the executive order's July 4 deadline.

vendors.name: Radiant Nuclear
vendors.fuel: HALEU TRISO (fabricated by Standard Nuclear, Oak Ridge TN)
vendors.status: First new reactor design to be tested in DOE's DOME test bed. First TRISO fuel tranche received 2026-07-01; five-phase campaign (criticality → heat/power → full power → 150 h unattended continuous operation) targeting completion Q3 2026.
vendors.funding_note: $300M Series D on top of a $165M Series C (May), total raised >$500M. Reactor factory foundation in Oak Ridge, TN in 2026.

vendors.name: Westinghouse
vendors.test_reactor: Scaled 3 MWt heat-pipe nuclear test reactor at INL DOME, testing from 2026
vendors.commercial: First-customer SRC pilot (CA$80M, target 2029) cancelled by Westinghouse in fall 2025 — eVinci refocused on space, defence and government applications. Penn State FRONTIER: NRC notice of intent filed 2025-02-17 for a construction permit for a 15 MWt eVinci-based research reactor at University Park, PA.
vendors.notes: The only one of the three with a published site-footprint figure — designed to produce 5 MWe on sites as small as two acres. Delivers 24/7 for eight-plus years without refuelling.
